# 1. Making better variables

```{r functions}
get_empirical_breakdown <- function(df, var) {
  df |>
    group_by(.data[[var]]) |>
    summarize(
      Policies         = n(),
      Policy_Share_Pct = round(n() / nrow(df) * 100, 2),
      Claim_Frequency  = round(sum(n_claims) / sum(policy.Exposure), 4),
      Avg_Severity     = round(sum(total_losses) / pmax(1, sum(n_claims)), 2),
      Total_Exposure   = round(sum(policy.Exposure), 2),
      Exposure_Share   = round(sum(policy.Exposure) / sum(df$policy.Exposure) * 100, 2),
      Total_Claims     = sum(n_claims),
      Total_Loss       = round(sum(total_losses), 2),
      Pure_Premium     = round(sum(total_losses) / sum(policy.Exposure), 2),
      .groups = "drop"
    )
}

vars_to_check <- c(
      "pet.Type",
      "owner.Location",
      "owner.PetCount",
      "pet.Gender",
      "owner.Channel",
      "policy.NBRB",
      "pet.Offspring"
)
breakdowns <- vars_to_check |>
  rlang::set_names() |>
  map(~ get_empirical_breakdown(df, .x))

breakdowns$owner.Location
breakdowns$pet.Type
breakdowns$pet.Offspring
(petcount_breakdown <- breakdowns$owner.PetCount)

```

```{r}
df <- df |>
  mutate(
    owner.PetCount_Rating = factor(
      case_when(
        owner.PetCount == 1 ~ "1",
        owner.PetCount == 2 ~ "2",
        owner.PetCount == 3 ~ "3",
        owner.PetCount == 4 ~ "4",
        owner.PetCount >= 5 ~ "5+"
      ),
      levels = c("1", "2", "3", "4", "5+") # '1' is the base/reference level
    )
  )
```
